open_points.subject: owner instruction for room-name and alias rules
open_points.text: The owner learns the rule from the governance; the owner interface does not show it.
open_points.question: What concrete governance artifact or action teaches the owner this rule, when must that happen, and what prevents an owner who has not received or acknowledged it from writing a prohibited name?
options: Require governance onboarding or acknowledgement before the owner can write names
Rely on the owner reading a named governance document without acknowledgement
Accept that the rule is advisory and that uninformed owners may write prohibited names
open_points.default_guess: Name a versioned governance document and require the owner to acknowledge its naming rule before using the relevant owner actions.

witness.initial: The owner uses the owner interface, which does not display the naming rule, and has not been given any concretely specified governance instruction.
events: The owner creates a room or alias containing a person's condition or health need.
Registry accepts the value because it checks no content.
The value reaches the agent through its projection.
outcomes: An implementation requires prior acknowledgement of the governance rule, so the owner uses a neutral name.
An implementation treats the governance as external reading with no delivery or acknowledgement, so the prohibited name is accepted and disclosed.
witness.observer: The owner, the agent and its AI provider

open_points.subject: first-release agent instruction for room-name and alias rules
open_points.text: until then the rule binds the owner, and the agent through the governance's instructions to it.
open_points.question: Before the second-release manifest description exists, who supplies the rule to the agent, through what concrete input or trust boundary, how is its version tied to the running Registry contract, and what happens when that instruction is absent or stale?
options: Kernel injects a versioned governance instruction into every agent session and blocks affected writes if it is missing
The owner supplies the instruction when approving each write
The agent is merely expected to have read governance text, with no runtime check
open_points.default_guess: Have Kernel inject a versioned instruction into every agent session and refuse room or alias writes when the required instruction version is unavailable.

witness.initial: The first release is running, so the manifest description has not yet been changed, and an agent session is granted a project.
events: The agent prepares an add-room request with a name such as "Bathroom for wheelchair".
Kernel submits the approved request to Registry.
Registry accepts it because Registry performs no content check.
outcomes: Kernel supplied the governance instruction, so the agent chooses a neutral room name.
No component supplied the unspecified governance instruction, so the prohibited name is stored and later reaches the agent and its AI provider.
witness.observer: The owner and the agent's AI provider
